KO.rationale: KO is a globally dominant, cash-generative franchise with exceptional brand equity (Brand Finance $46.3B, 32% YoY), an asset-light concentrate model delivering 61% gross margins, 26% net margins, and 40% ROE, plus a 64-year dividend-growth streak. Q1 2026 results showed accelerating momentum: organic revenue +10%, comparable EPS +18% YoY to $0.86 (beating consensus $0.81), and management raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $3.24–$3.27 (8–9% growth). However, the stock is not cheap: trailing PE of 27.2x sits in the upper half of its 12-month range (23.2–28.5x), and the 3.7% earnings yield trails the 10-year Treasury at 4.47% by 77bp — a meaningful headwind for a low-growth defensive in a rising-rate environment. The forward PE of ~24x implies consensus already prices in the guided EPS growth. Structural risks (CSD overdependence at 69% of volume, IRS tax litigation, sugar taxes, GLP-1 headwinds) are real but mitigated by portfolio diversification (Zero Sugar +14%, Fairlife, Costa). The BODYARMOR impairment ($960M) signals not every bet works. Price has been flat over the most recent quarter (-0.3%), offering no momentum signal. Net: a high-quality franchise fairly priced at a premium, with the valuation already reflecting the positive trajectory. Mildly positive on fundamentals and trajectory, but capped by valuation that leaves limited margin of safety.
